[[File:Carl Friedrich Gauss 1840 by Jensen.jpg|thumb|200px|Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855)]]

[[Carl Friedrich Gauss]] (1777–1855) is the [[eponym]] of all of the topics listed below. 
There are over 100 topics all named after this German mathematician and scientist, all in the fields of mathematics, physics, and astronomy. The English eponymous adjective ''Gaussian'' is pronounced {{IPAc-en|'|g|au|s|i|@n}}.<ref>{{cite book |editor-last=Wells |editor-first=John |editor-link=John C. Wells |title=Longman Pronunciation Dictionary |publisher=Pearson Longman |edition=3rd |year=2008 |isbn=978-1-4058-8118-0}}</ref>

== Mathematics ==
[[Image:Gaussian curvature.svg|thumb|Various Gaussian curvatures]]

=== [[Algebra]] and [[linear algebra]] ===
{{columns-list|colwidth=20em|
*[[Gaussian elimination]], also known as ''row reduction'' or ''Gaussian method''
*[[Gauss–Jordan elimination]]
*[[Gauss–Seidel method]]
*[[Cyclotomic polynomial#Gauss's formula|Gauss's cyclotomic formula]]
*[[Gauss's lemma (polynomial)|Gauss's lemma]] in relation to [[polynomial]]s
*[[Gaussian binomial coefficient]], also called ''Gaussian polynomial'' or ''Gaussian coefficient''
* [[Gauss transformation]], also called ''Frobenius matrix''
}}
=== [[Geometry]] and [[differential geometry]] ===
[[Image:Gauss map.svg|thumb|218x218px|Gauss map]]
{{columns-list|colwidth=20em|
*[[Gauss–Newton line#Theorem 3|Gauss–Bodenmiller theorem]] – described on [http://users.math.uoc.gr/~pamfilos/eGallery/problems/GaussBodenmiller.html website of University of Crete]
*[[Gauss–Bolyai–Lobachevsky space]], a [[hyperbolic geometry]]
*[[Gauss–Bonnet theorem]], a theorem about curvature in [[differential geometry]] for 2d surfaces
**[[Chern–Gauss–Bonnet theorem]] in differential geometry, [[Shiing-Shen Chern]]'s generalization of the above theorem to higher dimensions
*[[Gauss's braid]] in [[braid theory]] – a four-strand braid
*[[Gauss–Codazzi equations]]
*[[Gauss–Manin connection]], a connection on a vector bundle over a family of algebraic varieties
*[[Gauss–Newton line]] – described in [http://www.math.sjsu.edu/~alperin/11PointConic.pdf Journal for Geometry and Graphics], see also [[Newton line]]
*[[Gauss's area formula]]
*[[Gauss's lemma (Riemannian geometry)|Gauss's lemma]] in [[Riemannian geometry]]
*[[Gauss map]] in differential geometry
*[[Gaussian curvature]], defined in his [[Theorema egregium]]
* [[Gauss circle problem]]
}}

=== [[Number theory]] ===
[[File:Gaussian moat 15x15.svg|thumb|upright=1.35|Gaussian moat]]
{{columns-list|colwidth=20em|
*[[Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing constant]], a constant in [[number theory]]
*[[Gauss's constant]], the [[Multiplicative inverse|reciprocal]] of the [[arithmetic–geometric mean|AGM]] of 1 and <math>\scriptstyle\sqrt{2}</math>
*[[Gauss's digamma theorem]], a theorem about the [[digamma function]]
*[[Wilson's theorem#Gauss's generalization|Gauss's generalization of Wilson's theorem]]
*[[Gauss's lemma (number theory)|Gauss's lemma]] in [[number theory]]
*[[Gauss composition law]] – described on [http://www.dms.umontreal.ca/~andrew/PDF/AlgTalkSlides.pdf website of University of Université de Montréal]
*[[Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing operator#The Gauss map|Gauss map]] in number theory
*[[Gaussian moat]]
*[[class number problem|Gauss class number problem]] 
*[[Multiplication theorem#Gamma function–Legendre formula|Gauss's multiplication formula]]
}}

*[[Gaussian period]]
*[[Gaussian rational]]
*[[Gauss sum]], an [[exponential sum]] over [[Dirichlet character]]s

== Awards and recognitions ==
*[[Carl Friedrich Gauss Prize]], a mathematics award
*[[Gauss Lectureship]], a mathematical distinction
* The Gauss Mathematics Competition in Canadian junior high schools, an annual national mathematics competition administered by the [[Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing]]

== Other things named for him ==
=== Biology ===
[[file:Gaussia_maya4.jpg|thumb|160px|[[Gaussia maya]]]]
* ''[[Gaussia (plant)|Gaussia]]'', a palm genus described by [[Hermann Wendland]] with the then new species ''[[Gaussia princeps (plant)|Gaussia princeps]]'', collected by [[Charles Wright (botanist)|Charles Wright]] in western Cuba. Named in "memoriam astronomi Caroli Friderici Gauss".<ref>Wendland, H., 1865. Ueber die neue Palmengatung Gaussia. Nachr. Königl. Ges. Wiss. Georg-Augusts-Univ. 1865.</ref>
* ''[[Gaussia (crustacean)|Gaussia]]'', a genus of [[copepod]]s

=== Informatics ===
*[[Gaussian (software)|Gaussian]], a computational chemistry software program
*[[GAUSS (software)|GAUSS]]{{fact|date=February 2023}}, a matrix programming language for mathematics and statistics

== Place names and expedition named in his honour ==
[[File:Braunschweig Gaussberg von Suedwesten (2011).JPG|thumb|upright|The Gaussberg in [[Braunschweig|Braunschweig, Germany]] with the Gauss memorial in front]]
'''Terrestrial'''
*The [[Gauss expedition]], the first German expedition to Antarctica (1901–1903)
** The ship ''[[Gauss (ship)|Gauss]]'', used in the [[Gauss expedition]] to the Antarctic
* [[Gaussberg]] in Antarctica, an extinct volcano discovered by the Gauss expedition
* [[Mount Gauss]], in Antarctica 
* [[Gauss Peninsula]], East Greenland
* Gaussberg, a hill in [[Braunschweig]]

'''Celestial'''
* Crater [[Gauss (crater)|Gauss]] on the [[Moon]]<ref>Andersson, L. E.; Whitaker, E. A., (1982). NASA Catalogue of Lunar Nomenclature. NASA RP-1097.</ref>
* [[Asteroid]] [[1001 Gaussia]]

== Institutions and buildings named in his honour ==
* The ''Carl-Friedrich-Gauss Fakultät'' of [[Braunschweig University of Technology]]<ref>[https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/en/fk1 Carl-Friedrich-Gauß-Fakultät]</ref>
* Several schools in Germany named after Gauss
* Several buildings named "Gauss Haus" or "Gauss Building":
** [[Gauss Tower]], an observation tower in [[Dransfeld]], Germany
** The Gauss Building at the [[University of Idaho]] (College of Engineering)
** Gauss Haus, an [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|NMR]] center at the [[University of Utah]]
** The 'Gauss House', a common room in the University of Sussex Mathematical and Physical Sciences department.
** A dormitory building is named after him in [[Crown College, University of California, Santa Cruz|University of California, Santa Cruz, in Crown College]]

== Monuments, busts, and memorial plaques ==
Gauss Monuments were erected in Brunswick and Göttingen (the last together with Weber). [[Bust (sculpture)|Bust]]s of Gauss were placed in the [[Walhalla (memorial)|Walhalla]] hall of fame near [[Regensburg]] and in the [[GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences|German Research Centre for Geosciences]] in [[Potsdam]]. Several places where Gauss has stayed in Germany are marked with plaques.

<gallery>
File:Carl.Friedrich.Gauss.Bueste.vor1900.GFZ.jpg|Bust by ''Hans Weddo von Glümer'' (1895) in the [[GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences|German Research Centre for Geosciences]] in [[Potsdam]]<ref>{{cite journal | last = Reich | first = Karin | title = Bessel, Gauß und Baeyer: Drei Büsten im ehemalig Königlich Geodätischen Institut Potsdam, heute Helmert-Haus, im 'Wissenschaftspark Albert Einstein, Telegrafenberg Potsdam' | journal = Mitteilungen der Gauss-Gesellschaft | issue = 56 | pages = 67–74 | year = 2019 | language = de}}</ref>
File:Carl Friedrich Gauß, Büste von Friedrich Künkler, 001.jpg|Bust by Friedrich Künkler (1810)<ref>{{cite journal | last = Michling | first = Horst | title = Zur Gaußbüste von Friedrich Künkler | journal = Mitteilungen der Gauss-Gesellschaft | issue = 3 | pages = 3–4 | year = 1966 | language = de}}</ref>
File:Gauss Stein Wilseder Berg.jpg|Gauss memorial on the [[Wilseder Berg]], highest point in the [[Lüneburg Heath|Luneburg Heath]]
File:Walhalla wie Parthenon zu Ehren bedeutender Personen - erbaut 1842 - König Ludwig I - Foto Wolfgang Pehlemann DSCN2430.jpg|A bust of Gauss is placed in the Walhalla since 2007
</gallery>

== Other commemorations ==
Germany issued three postage stamps honoring Gauss, one in 1955 on the hundredth anniversary of his death and two others in 1977, the 200th anniversary of his birth.

<gallery>
File:DBP 1955 204 Carl Friedrich Gauß.jpg|Stamp (West Germany) 1955
File:DBP 1977 928 Carl Friedrich Gauß.jpg|Stamp (West Germany) 1977
File:Stamp Carl Friedrich Gauß.jpg|Stamp (East Germany) 1977
File:1856 Friedrich Brehmer Denkmünze auf Gauss nach Christian Heinrich Hesemann im Auftrag von Georg. V. von Hannover, Medaille Avers mit Portrait.jpg|Medal for Gauss (1856, front)
File:1856 Friedrich Brehmer Denkmünze auf Gauss nach Christian Heinrich Hesemann im Auftrag von Georg. V. von Hannover, Medaille Revers mit Efeukranz, Gipsmodell.jpg|Medal for Gauss (1856, back) "mathematicorum principi"
</gallery>
